## OLS and the Simulated ATE

Simulates nonlinear treatment effects and compares two robust OLS estimates with the true ATE of 2.

```{r}
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

set.seed(5280)
n <- 5000
W <- rnorm(n)
V <- rnorm(n)
D <- (W + V > 0) ## So the treatment satisfies unconfoundedness but not complete randomization
epsilon <- rnorm(n)
Y <- 1 + D + W + D * W^2 + sin(W) + epsilon ## ATE=2

fit_short <- lm(Y ~ D)
fit_longer <- lm(Y ~ D + W)
coeftest(fit_short, vcov. = vcovHC(fit_short, type = "HC2"))["D", ]
coeftest(fit_linear, vcov. = vcovHC(fit_long, type = "HC2"))["D", ]
```

## Causal-Forest AIPW Estimate

Fits a causal forest and reports its AIPW estimate of the simulated ATE.

```{r}
library(grf)
### Generate data. 
set.seed(5280)
n <- 3000      
p <- 12
W <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
D <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.4 + 0.2 * (W[, 1] > 0))
Y <- pmax(W[, 1], 0) * D + W[, 2] + pmin(W[, 3], 0) + rnorm(n)

# Plant a forest
forest <- causal_forest(W, Y, D, num.trees = 4000)

# Estimate the ATE
average_treatment_effect(forest,target.sample="all",method="AIPW")
```
